title: wish
subtitle: I wish you luck / I wish I knew / I wish it would stop
summary: Use wish somebody luck for good wishes, wish + past to regret how things are, and wish ... would to say you want something to happen or change.

lesson.heading: wish somebody luck
lesson.text: We say **wish somebody luck / all the best / success** etc. We say 'wish somebody something' (luck, happiness etc.), but we do not say 'I wish something happens'. We use **hope** in this situation.

examples.text: **I wish you** all the best in the future.
I saw Mark before the exam and he **wished me luck**.
I'm sorry you're not well. **I hope** you feel better soon.

left.label: wish somebody something
examples: **I wish you** a pleasant stay at this hotel.

right.label: hope (that) something happens
examples: **I hope you enjoy** your stay at this hotel. (not I wish you enjoy)

lesson.heading: wish + past = regret about now
lesson.text: We also use wish to say that we regret something - that something is not as we would like it. When we use wish in this way, we use the **past** (knew/lived etc.), but the meaning is present.

examples.text: **I wish I knew** what to do about the problem.
**I wish you didn't have** to go so soon.
Do you **wish you lived** near the sea?
examples.note: you don't live near the sea

examples.text: Jack's going on a trip to Mexico soon. **I wish I was going** too.

lesson.heading: wish + had done = regret about the past
lesson.text: To say that we regret something that happened before, we use **wish + had known / had said** etc.

examples.text: **I wish I'd known** about the party. I'd have gone if I'd known.
It was a stupid thing to say. **I wish I hadn't said** it.

lesson.heading: I wish I could / I wish I could have
lesson.text: **I wish I could** (do something) = I regret that I cannot do it. **I wish I could have** (done something) = I regret that I could not do it.

examples.text: I'm sorry you have to go. **I wish you could stay** longer.
I've met that man before. **I wish I could remember** his name.
I hear the party was great. **I wish I could have gone**.

lesson.heading: I wish ... would
lesson.text: It's been raining all day and Tanya doesn't like it. She would like the rain to stop, but this will probably not happen. We use **I wish ... would** when we would like something to happen or change, and often to complain about a situation. **I wish ... wouldn't** complains about things that people do repeatedly.

examples.text: The phone has been ringing for five minutes. **I wish somebody would answer** it.
**I wish you'd do** something instead of just sitting and doing nothing.
**I wish you wouldn't keep** interrupting me.

left.label: I wish ... would (I want it to happen)
examples: **I wish Sarah would come**. (= I want her to come)
**I wish somebody would buy** me a car.

right.label: I wish ... was/had (how I'd like things to be)
examples: **I wish Sarah was** (or were) here now. (not I wish Sarah would be)
**I wish I had** a car. (not I wish I would have)

lesson.text: Wish + would is for something you want to happen or change. For a state you'd like to be different, use wish + past (I wish I had / I wish I was).

exercises.prompt: Which word fills the gap in each sentence: wish or hope?

items.text: I ___ you a pleasant stay at this hotel.
Enjoy your holiday. I ___ you have a great time.
Goodbye. I ___ you all the best for the future.
We're going to have a picnic tomorrow, so I ___ the weather is nice.
Congratulations on your new job. I ___ you every success.
Good luck in your new job. I ___ it works out well for you.

exercises.prompt: I'm sorry you're not well. I ___ you feel better soon.
exercises.explanation: We say wish somebody something (luck etc.), but for 'something happens' we use hope.

exercises.prompt: It's a difficult question. I wish ___ the answer.
exercises.explanation: A regret about now takes the past after wish: I wish I knew.

exercises.prompt: I bought these shoes, but now I don't like them. I wish I ___ them.
exercises.explanation: A regret about something that happened before: wish + had done (I wish I hadn't bought them).

exercises.prompt: You're looking for a job - so far without success. Nobody will give you a job. Say what you wish.
exercises.answer: I wish somebody would give me a job.
exercises.explanation: You want something to happen, so use I wish ... would.

exercises.prompt: I wish ___. We've been waiting for 20 minutes.
exercises.explanation: You want something to happen: I wish ... would (I wish the bus would come).

exercises.statement: I wish Sarah would be here now.
exercises.explanation: I wish Sarah was (or were) here now. For how we'd like things to be, use wish + past, not would.

exercises.prompt: You're lucky to be going away. I wish ___ with you.
exercises.explanation: I wish I could = I regret that I cannot: I wish I could come with you.

exercises.prompt: Match each situation with what you say.

pairs.left: You're waiting for Jane. She's late and you're getting impatient.
pairs.right: I wish she would hurry up.

pairs.left: A dog has been barking for a long time and you're trying to study.
pairs.right: I wish that dog would stop barking.

pairs.left: Your friend always drives fast and you don't like this.
pairs.right: I wish you wouldn't drive so fast.

pairs.left: Joe leaves the door open all the time. This annoys you.
pairs.right: I wish you wouldn't leave the door open.

pairs.left: A lot of people drop litter in the street. You don't like this.
pairs.right: I wish people wouldn't drop litter.

pairs.left: It's raining. You want to go out, but not in the rain.
pairs.right: I wish it would stop raining.

exercises.statement: You keep interrupting me! I wish you wouldn't keep interrupting me.
exercises.explanation: Correct. I wish ... wouldn't complains about something a person does repeatedly.

exercises.prompt: I don't have a car and I'd love one. I wish I ___ a car.
exercises.explanation: This is how I'd like things to be, so wish + past (had), not wish ... would have.

exercises.prompt: When we were in London last year, we didn't have time to see all the things we wanted to see. I wish ___ there longer.
exercises.explanation: I wish I could have (done) = I regret that I could not do it in the past.
